Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with **finite** quantum characteristic $e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the residue set with integer residue labels $0,1,\dots,e-1$, and use the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type

derivations.claim: The associated graded. Give $x_i$ degree $1$ and the symmetric group degree $0$. By [F1] the transported relation has leading term $x_i^\ell$ with all other dot terms of total degree below $\ell$, and the bounded reduction sends monomials of dot degree $\le r$ to bounded monomials of dot degree $\le r$; independence of the bounded basis makes these the filtration steps $F_r$. The leading mixed relations give the variable permutation action of $S_d$, and the transported relations give $x_i^\ell=0$ in the associated graded. Hence the natural surjection $F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d \longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}H_d^\Lambda$ is an isomorphism: the bounded monomials of the truncated algebra map degree-by-degree onto the basis of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

Symmetric polynomials are central. For $x=x_i$, $y=x_{i+1}$, $s=s_i$ the relations of [F2] give, by induction on products, $sg(x,y)-g(y,x)s=\frac{g(y,x)-g(x,y)}{x-y}$ for every polynomial $g$; the quotient is a polynomial because the numerator vanishes at $x=y$. Applying this to a polynomial symmetric in $x,y$ shows that it commutes with $s$, and a globally symmetric polynomial commutes with every $s_i$ and every $x_j$, hence is central in $H_d^\Lambda$. No division by an integer or by $x-y$ inside the algebra is used. [F2, algebra]

Cycle coefficients in the graded centralizer. In $B=F[X_1,\dots,X_d]/(X_1^\ell,\dots,X_d^\ell)\rtimes FS_d$, put $h_r(I)=\sum X^b$ over $0\le b_i<\ell$ and $\sum_{i\in I}b_i=(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, and $A^{(r)}=h_r(I)A$ for a cycle $A$ on $I$, $0\le r<\ell$. For a coefficient $gA$ commuting with the $X_i$, the equations are $(X_i-X_{A(i)})g=0$. On one cycle they equate coefficients obtained by transferring one unit between consecutive coordinates, with out-of-range coefficients interpreted as zero. At fixed total degree, transfer units until the first $|I|-1$ coordinates are $\ell-1$. If the total is $(|I|-1)(\ell-1)+r$, every coefficient equals the coefficient at $(\ell-1,\dots,\ell-1,r)$; if the total is smaller, the same transfers reach a zero coordinate followed by a transfer to exponent $-1$, and all coefficients vanish. Thus the solutions on that cycle have basis $h_0(I),\dots,h_{\ell-1}(I)$. For disjoint cycles apply these equations separately to each coefficient in the monomial basis of the complementary variables; this gives exactly the products of disjoint colored cycles as the polynomial centralizer basis. This argument also covers $\ell=1$: the truncated polynomial ring is $F$, and its centralizer is $FS_d$. [step 1.1, algebra]

Reduced-degree powers. Write $f(t)=t^\ell+c_1t^{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_\ell$. The mixed relations give $x_{i+1}^\ell=s_ix_i^\ell s_i+\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}x_i^t x_{i+1}^{\ell-1-t}s_i$. Starting with $x_1^\ell=-\sum_{a=1}^\ell c_ax_1^{\ell-a}$, induction on $i$ shows that $x_i^\ell$ has filtration degree at most $\ell-1$ and symbol $Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1}$ there, where $Y_i=\sum_{j<i}(j\ i)^{(0)}$. For $k=p\ell+r$, $0\le r<\ell$, it follows that $x_i^k$ has filtration degree at most $p(\ell-1)+r$ and symbol $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^pX_i^r$. This is a reduced degree: the ordinary degree-$k$ symbol may be zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Orbit sums and colored-cycle multiplication. Conjugation permutes the basis of step 2.1, so its fixed vectors have basis the orbit sums $z_\lambda$, indexed by colored cycle types, including trivial color-zero fixed points to fill rank $d$. No averaging is used. If $|I\cap J|=c>0$, direct multiplication gives $h_r(I)h_s(J)=\ell^{c-1}h_{r+s+(c-1)(\ell-1)}(I\cup J)$. For $c=1$, fixing the exponents away from the common variable fixes its exponent uniquely and gives the asserted coefficient one. For $c=2$, the basic repeated-edge computation is $h_0(i,j)^2=\ell X_i^{\ell-1}X_j^{\ell-1}$: only equal complementary exponents survive, with exactly $\ell$ choices. Joining the remaining common variables successively reduces the general case to these two computations. Consequently disjoint colored cycles commute; two cycles meeting at one point multiply to their merged cycle of color $r+s$; when they meet in at least two points the product vanishes unless $r=s=0$, and otherwise is a scalar times disjoint cycles all of color $\ell-1$. Indeed the displayed exponent equals the maximal degree on the union when $c=2$, and exceeds it when $c>2$ and $\ell>1$; when $\ell=1$ every polynomial coefficient is one and the assertion reduces to ordinary cycle multiplication. Iterating gives disjoint-cycle reductions, never increasing the union of supports. [step 2.1, algebra]

The star-cycle expansion. Let $y_i(p\ell+r)$ be the sum of $(j_1\ \cdots\ j_p\ i)^{(r)}$ over ordered, distinct $j_1,\dots,j_p<i$, and let $y_i(0)=1$. Expanding $Y_i^p$, sequences with distinct leaves give precisely $y_i(p\ell)$: the product of the star transpositions is one cycle, with a unique ordered leaf sequence for each such cycle. Any repeated leaf uses at most $p$ vertices including $i$; at its first repetition the intersecting cycles have at least two common vertices, so step 3.1 turns the result into saturated (color $\ell-1$) disjoint cycles or zero. Further star factors preserve saturation by the one-point rule, or vanish by the multiple-point rule. The term $X_i^{\ell-1}$ is itself a saturated singleton containing $i$; choosing it anywhere in $(Y_i-c_1X_i^{\ell-1})^p$ has the same consequence and uses at most $p$ vertices. Thus this power equals $y_i(p\ell)$ plus saturated disjoint-cycle products on at most $p$ vertices, always with $i$ in their support. Multiplication by $X_i^r$ gives exactly $y_i(p\ell+r)$ when $r>0$, because it raises the color of the distinct-leaf cycle to $r$, while every saturated error containing $i$ vanishes. (For $\ell=1$ there is no $r>0$ case.) This proves the complete power-symbol formula, including $p=0$. [step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

Filtration descent. If $z\in Z(H_d^\Lambda)$ has filtration degree $D$, its degree-$D$ symbol lies in $Z(B)$. By step 5.1 it is a linear combination of degree-$D$ symbols of central symmetric evaluations $p_\mu$; subtract that same combination in $H_d^\Lambda$ to lower the filtration degree. Repeating terminates because degrees are nonnegative; in degree zero the same triangular basis applies, and the next filtration step is zero. Thus every central element is a symmetric-polynomial evaluation, and step 1.2 proves the reverse inclusion. Rank zero was handled separately. No division by $\ell$, $d!$ or the field characteristic occurs. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 5.1] ∎

This refutes the intermediate claim, not the center theorem (x_1+x_2 itself evaluates to s_1). Attempted closure by dropping the false sentence leaves no surjectivity argument: the coloured-cycle solution basis and filtration-lowering symmetric lifts must actually be proved. Missing prerequisite: local coloured-cycle orbit basis and triangular symmetric lift theorem, together with exact PBW. Owner must assign/authorize that construction preserving arbitrary characteristic. Refuter 1 remains escalated and risk open.

citations.quote: Let $R=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ with $\ell\ge1$, and let $H_n$ be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] at the first polynomial $\prod_a(X_1-U_a)$.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with $T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]): 1.

Let $R=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ with $\ell\ge1$, and let $H_n$ be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] at the first polynomial $\prod_a(X_1-U_a)$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is $$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$ The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.
For $n\ge1$ and $A,B\in M_n(R)$ over a commutative ring, $$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B).$$

derivations.claim: The trace and its dual basis. Define $\tau\colon H_n\to R$ by $\tau(\mathcal B)=1$ at the zero-dot identity word and $0$ at every other PBW basis element, extended $R$-linearly; by [F1] this is well defined over $R$ and after base change. Put $J_1=1$ and $J_i=q_H^{-1}T_{i-1}J_{i-1}T_{i-1}$ in the finite Hecke subalgebra; the $J_i$ are units. Define the second family $\mathcal C=\bigl\{T_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)} X_1^{c_1}\cdots X_n^{c_n}:0\le c_i<\ell,\ v\in S_n\bigr\},\qquad \delta(0)=0,\ \delta(c)=-1\ (c>0).$ The standard anti-involution fixing the presentation generators fixes each $X_i$, so $\mathcal B^*=\{T_vX^c\}$ is a basis; at each fixed profile $c$, multiplying the finite Hecke factor by the unit $J_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_n^{\delta(c_n)}$ is an invertible $R$-linear change of the finite Hecke basis. Hence $\mathcal C$ is an $R$-basis of $H_n$. [F1, construct]

Cyclicity for $X_1$ via the tower. At rank one the algebra is commutative, so cyclicity is immediate; for the induction assume $n\ge2$. Identify $H_{n-1}$ with the subalgebra on $X_1,\dots,X_{n-1},T_1,\dots,T_{n-2}$; its bounded words are a subset of $\mathcal B$. Put $v_k=s_{n-1}\cdots s_k$ for $1\le k<n$ and $v_n=1$; the decomposition $w=uv_k$ with $u\in S_{n-1}$ is length additive, so $\{X_n^aT_{v_k}:0\le a<\ell,\ 1\le k\le n\}$ is a left $H_{n-1}$-basis of $H_n$. Define the left-linear projection $E_n\colon H_n\to H_{n-1}$ to be $1$ on $X_n^0T_{v_n}$ and $0$ on the other basis elements, and $\tau_n=\tau_{n-1}\circ E_n$. With $V=T_{n-1}\cdots T_1$ and $U=(T_{n-1}-q_H+1)\cdots(T_1-q_H+1)$, the mixed relation gives $VX_1=X_nU$, and [F2] gives $VX_1^m=X_n^mU+J_m$, where every term of $J_m$ has total dot degree $m$ and $X_n$-degree between $1$ and $m-1$ (the leading branch transfers the full exponent, each correction transfers a strictly smaller positive exponent, and no variable above $n$ occurs). For $m\le\ell$ every lower exponent in $J_m$ is below $\ell$, so $E_n(J_m)=0$; likewise $E_n(X_n^mU)=0$ for $1\le m<\ell$. Multiplying the first-dot relation $f(X_1)=0$ by $V$ gives $0=X_n^\ell U+J_\ell+\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}c_m(X_n^mU+J_m)+c_0V$, and applying $E_n$ yields $E_n(X_n^\ell U)=0$, which completes the missing case $m=\ell$. To verify right $X_1$-linearity, test the displayed left tower basis $X_n^aT_{v_k}$. For $k\ge2$, $T_{v_k}$ and $X_n$ commute with $X_1$; its projection is zero unless $a=0,k=n$, where the equality is immediate. For $k=1$, $VX_1=X_nU$ gives $E_n(X_n^aVX_1)=E_n(X_n^{a+1}U)=0$ for $0\le a<\ell$: bounded positive exponents project to zero, and the endpoint $a+1=\ell$ was just established. Left $H_{n-1}$-linearity then extends the equality to every $h$. Hence $E_n(hX_1)=E_n(h)X_1$ for all $h$, and by left linearity $E_n(X_1h)=X_1E_n(h)$; induction on $n$ gives $\tau_n(X_1h)=\tau_n(hX_1)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

Cyclicity for the finite generators. Let $p=X^a$ be a bounded dot monomial and $w\in S_n$. By [F2], $T_jp=(s_jp)T_j+(1-q_H)X_{j+1}\frac{p-s_jp}{X_j-X_{j+1}};$ for $p=X_j^aX_{j+1}^b$ times the other variables, the correction monomials have the same total dot degree and both displayed exponents at most $\max(a,b)<\ell$ (the exponents run as $(a-1-k,b+1+k)$ or $(a+k,b-k)$), so when the exponent profile is positive every term on either side of $\tau(T_jpT_w)=\tau(pT_wT_j)$ has a positive bounded profile and evaluates to $0$. When $p=1$, the finite Hecke multiplication formula [F1] gives coefficient of $1$ in $T_jT_w$, respectively $T_wT_j$, equal to $q_H$ if $w=s_j$ and $0$ otherwise. This proves $\tau(T_jh)=\tau(hT_j)$ without using the trace one is proving. [F1, F2, algebra]

Generation and symmetry. The elements $X_1,T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ generate $H_n$ as an $R$-algebra: the constant term $c_0=(-1)^\ell\prod_aQ_a$ is a unit, so $f(X_1)=0$ makes $X_1^{-1}$ a polynomial in $X_1$; each $T_j^{-1}=q_H^{-1}(T_j-q_H+1)$; and $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$, with inverses expressed likewise. Moving the generators of a word one at a time around $\tau$, using steps 1.2 and 1.3, gives $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for every pair of words, hence for all $a,b$ by $R$-bilinearity; the pairing $(a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)$ is associative and symmetric. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

Restricted-profile zero values. For $0\le j\le n$ let $U_j$ be the span of the PBW words whose dot entries above $j$ vanish, all finite permutations included. It is a right finite-Hecke module. Multiplying its dot part by any polynomial in $X_1,\dots,X_j$ stays in $U_j$: transport the first cyclotomic relation successively only through $T_1,\dots,T_{j-1}$, so each resulting relation reduces a power of $X_i$, $i\le j$, using variables of index at most $i$ and finite words of indices below $i$; repeated Bernstein straightening and the bounded reduction of [F1] therefore never introduce a variable above $j$. In particular $U_j$ is the dot algebra on its first $j$ variables times the finite Hecke algebra. For $1\le k<\ell$ and $h\in U_j$, $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=0$, directly from the bounded basis, since the new exponent is positive and bounded. This statement concerns $h\in U_j$, rather than arbitrary $h\in H_n$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Transferred restricted-profile powers. Write $q=q_H$. For $1\le i\le j+1\le n$, $1\le k\le\ell$ and $h\in U_j$ we claim $\tau(X_{j+1}^kh)=q^{i-j-1}\tau(T_j\cdots T_iX_i^kT_i\cdots T_jh)$, with empty chains when $i=j+1$. The mixed relations give $X_i^k=q^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}^kT_{i-1}+q^{-1}(q-1)\sum_{c=1}^{k-1}X_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}$, by induction on $k$ using that $T_{i-1}$ commutes with $X_{i-1}X_i$. To descend from $i$ to $i-1$, it suffices to show every correction has trace zero. Put $A=T_j\cdots T_i$, $B=T_i\cdots T_j$. For $0<c<k$, the mixed relation and the formula $X_{j+1}=q^{i-j-1}AX_iB$ give the exact identity $AX_i^cX_{i-1}^{k-c}T_{i-1}Bh=q^{j-i+1}AX_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}X_{i-1}h$: substitute $B=q^{j-i+1}X_i^{-1}A^{-1}X_{j+1}$ and use $X_iT_{i-1}X_i^{-1}=X_{i-1}^{-1}T_{i-1}X_{i-1}$. Expand $X_i^{c-1}X_{i-1}^{k-c-1}T_{i-1}A^{-1}$ in the reversed PBW order $\sum a_{w,b}T_wX^b$ using $T_a^{-1}=q^{-1}(T_a+1-q)$. Bernstein straightening swaps the two exponents or replaces them by intermediate exponents, so every exponent stays nonnegative and at most $\max(c-1,k-c-1)\le k-2$; variables have index at most $j+1$. Cyclicity from step 2.1 makes the trace of each correction a sum of traces of $X_{j+1}^{1+b_{j+1}}(X_1^{b_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j})X_{i-1}hAT_w$. The parenthesized remaining factor lies in $U_j$ by step 2.2, and $1\le1+b_{j+1}\le k-1<\ell$, so each trace is zero. Downward induction proves the claim, including $k=1$, whose correction sum is empty. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

The cyclotomic endpoint. Apply step 3.1 with $i=1$, $k=\ell$. In $\tau(q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1X_1^\ell T_1\cdots T_jh)$ replace $X_1^\ell$ using its first cyclotomic relation. Each positive power $X_1^k$, $k<\ell$, transfers back to $X_{j+1}^k$ by step 3.1 and contributes zero by step 2.2. The constant term contributes $\alpha\tau(J_{j+1}h)$, where $\alpha=-f(0)=(-1)^{\ell+1}Q_1\cdots Q_\ell$ and $J_{j+1}=q^{-j}T_j\cdots T_1T_1\cdots T_j$. Thus $\tau(X_{j+1}^\ell h)=\alpha\tau(hJ_{j+1})$ for every $h\in U_j$. For $j=0$ this follows directly from the first polynomial; for $\ell=1$ there are no positive-power intermediate terms. The restriction on $h$ is essential. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

The full Gram blocks. Let $\mathcal B_j$ and $\mathcal C_j$ be the parts of the two bases with entries above $j$ zero, and let $G_j=(\tau(bc))$ be their matrix, of size $N_j=\ell^jn!$. For new profiles $b,c$ at position $j+1$, cyclicity and commuting dots rewrite an entry as $\tau(X_{j+1}^{b+c}hJ_{j+1}^{\delta(c)})$, where $h=X_1^{b_1+c_1}\cdots X_j^{b_j+c_j}T_wT_vJ_1^{\delta(c_1)}\cdots J_j^{\delta(c_j)}\in U_j$ by step 2.2; earlier combined exponents may exceed $\ell-1$, and that same reduction argument is why this remains in $U_j$. If $b=c=0$ the block is $G_j$. If $0<b+c<\ell$ it is zero by step 2.2. If $b+c=\ell$, then $c>0$ and step 4.1 cancels the last $J_{j+1}^{-1}$, giving the block $\alpha G_j$. Order rows by $b=0,1,\dots,\ell-1$ and columns by $c=0,\ell-1,\dots,1$. The row and column at zero have only $G_j$ at their intersection. Among positive rows and columns the blocks above the diagonal have $b+c<\ell$ and vanish, the diagonal has $b+c=\ell$, and blocks below may be arbitrary. Hence $G_{j+1}$ is block lower triangular with diagonal $G_j,\alpha G_j,\dots,\alpha G_j$, so $\det G_{j+1}=\pm\alpha^{(\ell-1)N_j}(\det G_j)^\ell$. At $j=0$, $G_0=(\tau(T_wT_v))$ has entry $q^{\operatorname{length}(w)}\delta_{v,w^{-1}}$ by [F1], and its determinant is a unit. Induction gives a unit determinant for $G_n$; since $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$ are bases, the pairing identifies $H_n$ with its $R$-dual. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, algebra]

Base change and boundary cases. Presentation base change commutes with forming $H_n$, and the universal PBW basis is free, so the trace coefficients and the inverse Gram matrix base-change to any commutative ring in which all parameters remain units; in particular they do so for the LM deformation DVR with $q_Ht$ and $Q_at^{na}$. For $n=0$ use $H_0=R$ with $\tau(1)=1_R$; for $\ell=1$ the family $\mathcal C$ consists of finite $T_v$ and the same proof applies. The separate level-zero positive-rank quotient is $0$, with the zero perfect pairing, and no claim $\tau(1)=1$ is made for it. No generic faithfulness or imported Bremke–Malle trace statement is used. [step 1.1, step 5.1] ∎

risk_review.notes: Read all six steps and exact PBW/finite-Hecke/determinant supplier interfaces. Archived comparison confirms the repaired q_H decreasing-length coefficient, earlier 1.3 citation, and tower proof for X_1 cyclicity. The tower endpoint E_n(X_n^ℓ U)=0 follows from the transported first-dot relation; the finite-generator cyclicity uses bounded positive profiles and is valid. However 2.2 asserts τ(X_(j+1)^ℓ h)=ατ(hJ_(j+1)) and zero off-diagonal blocks for arbitrary earlier profiles and all permutations without a restricted-profile computation. Step 1.2 alone only supplies a special tower projection identity. Attempted closure by direct rank-two reduction agrees with the asserted identity in small corners but does not establish all earlier dot profiles or the triangular blocks. Exact PBW is itself unresolved upstream. Missing result: a full restricted-profile trace identity and Gram-block calculation, or a proved equivalent unimodular dual basis. Owner must assign that substantial construction before perfectness and its annihilator consumers are accepted. Additionally the supplied Malle–Mathas reference URL math/0604108 is actually Mathas’s Seminormal forms and Gram determinants; the cited title/15-page locator is mismatched. Primary author bibliography identifies the intended article at DOI 10.1006/jabr.1997.7339; source identity needs correction. No source’s trace theorem replaces the missing local proof. Both touched and refuter 6 remain open.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda$ be the set of partitions
of $n$ ordered by dominance $\unrhd$
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), and for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let
$T(\lambda)=\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ be the set of standard $\lambda$-tableaux
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). Then the **Murphy basis
theorem** holds: the family
$$\mathcal M=\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$$
is an $R$-basis of $H$, and $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ is a cellular basis of $H$ in
the sense of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Explicitly:
(i) $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all $\lambda$ and $s,t$; and (ii) for every
$\lambda$, every $t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ and every $h\in H$ there exist
$r_v\in R$ with
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}},$$
where $H^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the $m_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. The
theorem holds over every commutative coefficient ring with $q\in R^{\times}$
and assumes no semisimplicity; the total number of Murphy elements is
$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}|\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)|^2=n!$
([[cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers]]), matching the rank of $H$.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation

$$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition
$(i\ i+1)$. For
$n=0,1$, the trivial group has the empty presentation.

For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary
finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the
permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type
$\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape. It has a Specht
filtration with multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$ of the
ordinary Specht module $S^\lambda$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). The row-double-coset
membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over
the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the
$\rho$-row parabolic in $S^\lambda$. Moreover the explicit ordinary Garnir
row-coset identity, the additive nonstandard-tableau factorization and the
same-column generator refinement
$$T_am_{st}\equiv-m_{st}+\sum_{u\lhd s}c_um_{ut}\pmod{\text{higher shapes}}$$
hold; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape
terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved
ordinary Murphy dominance ideals
([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]],
[[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]); the finite Garnir
algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that
dominance refinement.

For every $n\ge0$,
$$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}(f^\lambda)^2=n!,$$
where $f^\lambda$ is the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux and
$f^\varnothing=1$, $0!=1$.

derivations.claim: Finite-generator straightening. Every component-preserving row-standard multitableau factors its distinguished permutation into a permutation inside the contiguous component intervals followed by the unique shuffle of the intervals preserving internal order; the two inversion sets are disjoint, so the factorization is length-additive. Multiplying by $u_\lambda$ (which commutes with the Hecke generators internal to the intervals), ordinary Murphy straightening applies in each component; higher ordinary component shapes preserve component sizes and strictly increase multipartition dominance, and the final component shuffle relabels each component by an increasing list whose selected entries at any cutoff are an initial segment, so tableau-prefix inequalities are exactly the ordinary ones at the corresponding initial-segment length. For a fixed initial left row and right multiplication by $T_i$: if $ts_i$ is standard the length formula gives the usual standard term (or $q_H$ times it plus $(q_H-1)m_{t^\lambda t}$); if $i,i+1$ share a row the result is $q_Hm$; and if they share a component but the interchange fails standardness, factoring out the increasing component shuffle and applying the ordinary cell law gives same-shape terms with the same initial left row and strictly higher multipartition terms, the required transfer identity $T_cT_i=T_jT_c$ following from $cs_i=s_jc$ and the length/quadratic formula. A cross-component column failure is impossible because column standardness is imposed componentwise. Descending induction over a linear extension of multipartition dominance therefore makes each $N^{\ge\lambda}$ and $N^{>\lambda}$ stable under all finite generators; multiplying on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ and applying $*$ makes the higher spans two-sided ideals. This induction concerns spanning sets only and assumes no independence.

The cyclotomic component shift. Let $a=(a_k)$ with $a_k=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$ and $u_a=u_\lambda$, and let $b=a+e_k$. Put $u_b=u_a(X_{a_k+1}-Q_k)$; the factors commute, and for $a=a_k$ the defining recurrence gives the exact identity $u_aT_a\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_a=q_H^a igl(Q_ku_a+u_b igr),$ by substituting $T_a\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_a=q_H^aX_{a+1}$ and adding/subtracting $Q_ku_a$; the case $a=0$ is included. For $k>1$ form the multicomposition $
u$ obtained by appending a singleton row to component $k-1$ and deleting the first node of the first row of component $k$. Its cumulative sizes are $b$, so $u_
u=u_b$, and its Young subgroup is contained in $S_\lambda$; the left length-additive coset expansion gives $x_\lambda u_b=\sum_vT_v^*m_
u$. Sorting the rows of $
u$ in each component conjugates its Young subgroup and gives $m_
u=T_dm_{\operatorname{sort}
u}T_d^{-1}$ with $u_
u$ commuting with the component-preserving permutation, so the ordinary row-sorting argument expresses each term in standard pairs of shapes at least $\operatorname{sort}
u$, which strictly dominates $\lambda$: the cumulative total through component $k-1$ strictly increases and no later cumulative sum decreases. Hence $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. For $k=1$, nonemptiness of component $1$ forces $a_s\ge1$ for all $s\ge2$, so $u_b$ contains every factor $(X_1-Q_s)$ and vanishes by the cyclotomic relation; again $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$.

Right multiplication by $X_1$. Let $t$ be standard with entry $1$ in component $k$, an initial node, and initial label $a+1$ with $a=a_k$. Then $d(t)=(s_a\cdots s_1)w$ with $w$ fixing $1$ and $\ell(d(t))=a+\ell(w)$: pulling label $a+1$ to value $1$ crosses exactly the $a$ smaller initial labels, whose final values exceed $1$. A permutation fixing $1$ has a reduced word in $s_2,\dots,s_{n-1}$, so $T_w$ commutes with $X_1$. Multiplying the identity of step 1.2 on the right by $(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}$ and then by $T_w$ gives $m_\lambda T_{d(t)}X_1=q_H^aQ_km_\lambda(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w +q_H^ax_\lambda u_b(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w,$ whose second term lies in $N^{>\lambda}$ by step 1.2 and finite-generator stability, and whose first term lies modulo $N^{>\lambda}$ in the fixed-initial-row span. Hence that span is stable under $X_1$; multiplying on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ and using the left stability of the higher shapes gives the coefficient-independence law $m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$ first for each generator and then for every word, with coefficients independent of $s$, and $*$ makes the higher spans two-sided. Since $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ and the cyclotomic constant term is a unit when the $Q_a$ are invertible, these generators generate the Laurent affine quotient.

Spanning and cellularity. The smallest multipartition $\omega=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$ satisfies $u_\omega=x_\omega=m_\omega=1$, so the generator-stable span of the standard $m_{st}$ contains $1$ and is all of $H_n$: the Murphy family spans. By [[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], $H_n$ is independently free of rank $\ell^nn!$. Counting standard pairs with the ordinary identity $\sum_{\rho\vdash m}f_\rho^2=m!$ at the component sizes $n_a$ contributes $(n!)^2/\prod_an_a!$, and summing over the multipartition compositions gives $\ell^nn!$ by the multinomial theorem. The spanning family therefore has exactly the independent rank; its coefficient matrix in the ordered PBW basis is square and surjective between free modules, hence invertible, so the family is an $R$-basis and the proved involution and coefficient-independence laws are actual cellularity. Tensoring the proved basis and presentation supplies every commutative specialization with unit parameters, including repeated charges and the LM deformation DVR; no generic-flatness inference is made. Rank zero is the singleton empty basis.

Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 establish the generator-stable higher ideals for the finite-generator subalgebra; step 2.1 extends stability to $X_1$ and hence to all polynomial generators and gives the coefficient-independence law with two-sided higher spans; and step 3.1 proves that the standard Murphy family is an $R$-basis of exactly the independent rank, so that the involution and coefficient laws are cellularity in the sense of the Definition. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters inherits the basis and the cell law. No primitive-block classification is used.

basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$
with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$ independent of $s$. The higher spans are

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

derivations.claim: Initial-row eigenvalues. For component $k$ and $a=a_k$, [F1] gives $m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. The internal finite Hecke submodule generated by $m_\lambda$ modulo higher global shapes is spanned by standard internal component permutations; each such permutation fixes the smallest internal label $a+1$ (that label occupies the first node of its component), so its Hecke element has a reduced word in the internal generators with indices at least $a+2$ and commutes with $X_{a+1}$. Hence $X_{a+1}$ acts as the scalar $Q_k$ on that whole submodule, with errors in the two-sided ideal $N^{>\lambda}$. The $X$-recurrence then identifies $X_{a+i}$ on this submodule with $Q_k$ times the ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy element $M_i$ of [F2], by induction from the finite quadratic relation and the additive-JM recurrence (a polynomial identity also at $q_H=1$). Ordinary JM triangularity gives diagonal $Q_kq_H^{c-r}$ at the node $(r,c,k)$ occupied by local entry $i$: the internal label $i$ is not a row index, and no extra subtraction of $i-1$ occurs. For the initial component tableau, which is maximal in tableau dominance, there are no strictly more dominant same-shape terms. Thus for the node $(r,c,k)$ carrying global entry $t$, $m_\lambda X_t\equiv Q_kq_H^{c-r}m_\lambda\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$.

JM triangularity for every standard multitableau. Inducting through a reduced word of $w$, the relations [F1] give $T_wX_r=X_{w(r)}T_w+\sum_{v<w}\sum_ba_{(v,b)}X_bT_v,$ where the corrections are supported on proper Bruhat subwords (at the first correction a generator is deleted, moving its linear $X$-coefficient through preceding generators deletes further generators, and finite quadratic multiplication preserves Bruhat support). Applying this with $w=d(t)$ and multiplying by $m_\lambda$ on the left, step 1.1 evaluates every surviving $X$ coefficient modulo higher shapes; a correction $m_\lambda T_v$ reduces first to a row-standard representative $d(u)$ of its Young-subgroup coset, the removed row subgroup contributing its row eigenvalue, with $d(u)\le v<d(t)$; the Bruhat/tableau-prefix relation on the ordered rows of all components then makes $u$ strictly dominate $t$, and componentwise straightening of $u$ keeps the shape or produces same-shape tableaux at least $u$ in prefix dominance, hence strictly dominating $t$. The leading eigenvalue is $Q_kq_H^{j-i}$ at the node carrying $r$, because $w(r)$ is its initial-row label under $t=t^\lambda\cdot w=w^{-1}\cdot t^\lambda$. Therefore $m_{(t^\lambda,t)}X_r\equiv Q_kq_H^{j-i}m_{(t^\lambda,t)} +\sum_{v\lhd t}a_vm_{(t^\lambda,v)}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}},$ the exact arbitrary-level JM content statement, independent of an affine center theorem, semisimplicity or block classification. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

Residue words and boundary cases. On the resulting Specht module a total ordering extending tableau dominance triangularizes all the $X_r$ simultaneously; the one-dimensional successive quotients have exactly the content characters of step 2.1, so every simultaneous generalized eigenword is among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i\pmod e$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] for the ordinary part); the residue multiplicities of every such word equal the node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$, since permuting the labels of a standard tableau does not change the multiset of node residues. For rank zero, $H=F$, the sole shape and tableau are empty and all assertions have their one-dimensional interpretation. The triangularity is polynomial in the parameters, so it specializes to the LM deformation DVR and to the generic fibre.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

derivations.claim: Initial-row eigenvalues. For component $k$ and $a=a_k$, [F1] gives $m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. The internal finite Hecke submodule generated by $m_\lambda$ modulo higher global shapes is spanned by standard internal component permutations; each such permutation fixes the smallest internal label $a+1$ (that label occupies the first node of its component), so its Hecke element has a reduced word in the internal generators with indices at least $a+2$ and commutes with $X_{a+1}$. Hence $X_{a+1}$ acts as the scalar $Q_k$ on that whole submodule, with errors in the two-sided ideal $N^{>\lambda}$. The $X$-recurrence then identifies $X_{a+i}$ on this submodule with $Q_k$ times the ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy element $M_i$ of [F2], by induction from the finite quadratic relation and the additive-JM recurrence (a polynomial identity also at $q_H=1$). Ordinary JM triangularity gives diagonal $Q_kq_H^{c-r}$ at the node $(r,c,k)$ occupied by local entry $i$: the internal label $i$ is not a row index, and no extra subtraction of $i-1$ occurs. For the initial component tableau, which is maximal in tableau dominance, there are no strictly more dominant same-shape terms. Thus for the node $(r,c,k)$ carrying global entry $t$, $m_\lambda X_t\equiv Q_kq_H^{c-r}m_\lambda\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$.

JM triangularity for every standard multitableau. Inducting through a reduced word of $w$, the relations [F1] give $T_wX_r=X_{w(r)}T_w+\sum_{v<w}\sum_ba_{(v,b)}X_bT_v,$ where the corrections are supported on proper Bruhat subwords (at the first correction a generator is deleted, moving its linear $X$-coefficient through preceding generators deletes further generators, and finite quadratic multiplication preserves Bruhat support). Applying this with $w=d(t)$ and multiplying by $m_\lambda$ on the left, step 1.1 evaluates every surviving $X$ coefficient modulo higher shapes; a correction $m_\lambda T_v$ reduces first to a row-standard representative $d(u)$ of its Young-subgroup coset, the removed row subgroup contributing its row eigenvalue, with $d(u)\le v<d(t)$; the Bruhat/tableau-prefix relation on the ordered rows of all components then makes $u$ strictly dominate $t$, and componentwise straightening of $u$ keeps the shape or produces same-shape tableaux at least $u$ in prefix dominance, hence strictly dominating $t$. The leading eigenvalue is $Q_kq_H^{j-i}$ at the node carrying $r$, because $w(r)$ is its initial-row label under $t=t^\lambda\cdot w=w^{-1}\cdot t^\lambda$. Therefore $m_{(t^\lambda,t)}X_r\equiv Q_kq_H^{j-i}m_{(t^\lambda,t)} +\sum_{v\lhd t}a_vm_{(t^\lambda,v)}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}},$ the exact arbitrary-level JM content statement, independent of an affine center theorem, semisimplicity or block classification. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

Residue words and boundary cases. On the resulting Specht module a total ordering extending tableau dominance triangularizes all the $X_r$ simultaneously; the one-dimensional successive quotients have exactly the content characters of step 2.1, so every simultaneous generalized eigenword is among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i\pmod e$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] for the ordinary part); the residue multiplicities of every such word equal the node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$, since permuting the labels of a standard tableau does not change the multiset of node residues. For rank zero, $H=F$, the sole shape and tableau are empty and all assertions have their one-dimensional interpretation. The triangularity is polynomial in the parameters, so it specializes to the LM deformation DVR and to the generic fibre.

citations.quote: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]).

Let $R:=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ be the universal Laurent parameter ring of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], and let $H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the $R$-algebra presented there by the commuting units $X_1,\dots,X_n$, the generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the quadratic, braid, distant, Bernstein and mixed-commutation relations — **witho

For $H_n$ in [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all $\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a basis and a dominance-cellular datum: $$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$ with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$

For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis $$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$ where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type $\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with $T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]): 1.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation $$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$ where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition $(i\ i+1)$.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$ acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$ carrying $r$.

derivations.claim: The affine expansion with only variable-difference denominators. Writing $T_w$ as the product of the $\Phi_i$ and the scalars $c_{i,i+1}$ along a reduced word of $w$ and moving a Laurent polynomial $f$ leftward across the $\Phi$'s by [F2] expresses $T_wf$ as a sum of terms $c_v\,v(f)$ times a monomial in a subword, where $v$ runs over products of subwords of that reduced word, every denominator of $c_v$ is a product of differences $X_i-X_j$, and each $v$ is Bruhat-below $w$ by the subword characterization of Bruhat order ([F6]). In particular applying this with $f=u_\lambda$ keeps all denominators among the variable differences and introduces no $U_a-U_b$, quantum factorial, or Gram determinant. [F1, F2, F6, algebra]

Flagging is Bruhat-downward closed and gives monic divisibility. Let $S$ be semistandard of shape $\lambda$ and type $\mu$, and for a permutation $\sigma$ let $\pi=\sigma^{-1}$ map each label to its physical position; set $A_k=\sum_{a<k}|\lambda^{(a)}|$ and $B_k=\sum_{a<k}|\mu^{(a)}|$. By [F1] the flag condition says that a label of component $a$ occupies only a physical component $b\le a$, i.e. $\#\{r\le B_k:\pi(r)\le A_k\}=B_k$ for all $k$. The count is at most $B_k$; inversion preserves the Bruhat order and a Bruhat-smaller permutation has at least as many entries in every prefix rectangle, so every Bruhat-smaller permutation of a flagged one is flagged. If $\sigma$ is flagged then $\sigma(u_\lambda)=\prod_k\prod_{j\le A_k}(X_{\sigma(j)}-U_k)$ contains the factor $(X_r-U_k)$ for every $r\le B_k$, because $\pi(r)\le A_k$; hence $\sigma(u_\lambda)=u_\mu\prod_j\prod_{a(j)<k\le b(j)}(X_j-U_k)$ with $a(j)$ the physical component of the position occupied by label $j$ and $b(j)$ its type component, a monic polynomial. In particular $u_\mu$ divides $\sigma(u_\lambda)$ in the Laurent polynomial ring. [F1, F6, algebra]

The left row-double-coset identity and localized membership. Let $s_0$ be the least standard refinement of $S$ and $D=S_\mu d(s_0)^{-1}S_\lambda$. Every row-standard refinement of the semistandard $S$ is standard, and the ordinary length-additive left row-double-coset expansion gives $\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in D}T_w$, each element of $D$ exactly once, with no row-intersection quantum factorial ([F4] proves the identical finite identity; [F1] fixes the elements $T_{d(s)}^*$ and $x_\lambda$). Since $S_\mu$ permutes labels inside $\mu$-components and $S_\lambda$ permutes positions inside $\lambda$-rows, every $w\in D$ is flagged; hence every Bruhat-subword permutation $v$ in the expansion of step 1.1 is flagged by step 1.2, so $v(u_\lambda)=u_\mu g_v$ with $g_v$ a Laurent polynomial, and $T_wu_\lambda\in u_\mu H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}[(X_i-X_j)^{-1}]$ for every $w\in D$. Writing $b_0:=\sum_{w\in D}T_w$ and summing, $b_0u_\lambda\in u_\mu H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}[(X_i-X_j)^{-1}]$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

The flagged span is a right ideal and a left parabolic module. Let $W_\mu$ be the $R$-span of the $m_{st}$ with $s$ $\mu$-flagged. Right multiplication by a finite generator $T_i$ uses the Murphy expansion of [F3]: same-shape terms retain the left tableau, and higher terms arise from ordinary straightening inside physical components whose permutations are products of $d(s)$ with permutations internal to the physical intervals, hence only permute the admissible $\mu$-labels among the nodes of each component; the exact quadratic expansion, row normalization, and straightening inside components preserve the flagged set. Right multiplication by $X_1$ keeps the same-shape term and, in the higher component-shift term of the proved formula, moves one node of physical component $k$ to component $k-1$ with its $\mu$-component label unchanged: in cumulative-profile form the boundary $A_{k-1}$ increases by one and no other boundary decreases, so every previously valid rank rectangle of step 1.2 stays valid, and sorting and subsequent finite straightening happen inside the new component intervals; the $k=1$ term vanishes. For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation $$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$ where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition $(i\ i+1)$.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

u)$ identifies $$\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(M_

u,$$ with $R$-basis the rectangular sums $m_{(S,T)

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az\text{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]]). Its set of isomorphism classes is denoted $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)$. The **Grothendieck group** of $\mathcal C$ is $$ G_0(\mathcal C):=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)]\big/\langle e_Y-e_X-e_Z:\ 0\to X\to Y\to Z\to 0\text{ is short exact in }\mathcal C\rangle.
Any two composition series of a module have the same length, and their simple factors agree up to permutation and isomorphism.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$ acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$ carrying $r$.

derivations.claim: Centers and blocks of an endomorphism algebra containing the regular module. Let $M$ be a finite right $H$-module containing $H$ as a direct summand with projection $e$, and $C=\operatorname{End}_H(M)$. Then $eCe=\operatorname{End}_H(H)\cong H$ by left multiplication, and $Ce\cong\operatorname{Hom}_H(H,M)\cong M$ by evaluation at $1$. If $c\in Z(C)$, then $c$ restricts on the $H$-summand to left multiplication by some $h$; for each $m\in M$ the $H$-map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto ma$, is the off-diagonal block $j f_m\pi\in C$ through $H$, and commuting it with $c$ and evaluating at $1$ gives $c(m)=mh$. Since $c$ is $H$-linear, $c(ab)=c(a)b$ for $a,b\in H$ gives $ab h=ahb$, so with $a=1$ we get $hb=bh$ and $h\in Z(H)$. Conversely every $h\in Z(H)$ defines the $H$-linear endomorphism $m\mapsto mh$, which commutes with every $H$-endomorphism of $M$, hence is central in $C$. These constructions are inverse unital algebra maps, so $Z(C)\cong Z(H)$ and primitive central idempotents correspond bijectively ([F4]). For $M=\bigoplus_\lambda M_\lambda$ we have $M_\omega=H_n$, so this applies with $e=e_\omega$. [F1, F4, algebra]

Schur standards and nonzero heads. By [F2] the right cell module $\Delta_\lambda$ of $C_n$ has basis the $v_T$ over semistandard $T$ of shape $\lambda$. The unique tableau $T^\lambda$ of shape and type $\lambda$ gives $\varphi_{(T^\lambda,T^\lambda)}=e_\lambda$, the identity projection onto $M_\lambda$, an actual idempotent; evaluating the cell form at $v_{T^\lambda}$ gives $\langle v_{T^\lambda},v_{T^\lambda}\rangle=1$, so every standard is nonzero with nonzero form. Applying the finite cellular-head theory [F3] to $C_n$ (finite-dimensional and cellular over $F$ by [F2]) shows every head $L_\lambda=\Delta_\lambda/\mathrm{rad}\,\Delta_\lambda$ is nonzero, absolutely simple, the $L_\lambda$ are pairwise distinct and exhaust the simple $C_n$-modules, and $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]\ne0$ implies $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ with $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\lambda]=1$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

Split quasiheredity by an explicit heredity chain. Order the multipartitions in a linear extension of dominance and remove the maximal remaining cell layers successively; in the relevant quotient algebra $B$ the next layer $J$ has basis $c_{st}$ with a distinguished index $u$ whose Gram value is $G(u,u)=1$. Then $e=c_{uu}$ is idempotent, $c_{su}c_{ut}=c_{st}$, and the multiplication map $Be\otimes_FeB\to J$ is an isomorphism on these basis elements; also $eBe=Fe$, since the cell law and maximality of $J$ show every $ebe$ is a scalar multiple of $e$. Hence $Be$ is projective, $J$ is a direct sum of copies of $Be$, and $e\,\mathrm{rad}(B)\,e=0$ because the corner is a field. Thus $J$ is a split heredity ideal, and iterating gives a split heredity chain whose standards are the cell modules $\Delta_\lambda$; so $C_n$ is split quasihereditary over $F$. [F2, F3, algebra]

Weight dimensions and the unitriangular Kostka matrix. The weight projections $e_
u=\varphi_{(T^
u,T^
u)}$ are self-adjoint because $\varphi_{ST}^*=\varphi_{TS}$ ([F2]), and the cell action gives $v_Te_
u=\delta_{\operatorname{type}(T),
u}v_T$, so $\dim\Delta_\lambda e_
u$ is the number $K_{(\lambda,
u)}$ of semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $
u$; this already shows the standards and their forms are defined over the universal ring, free on the $v_T$. A semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$ and type $
u$ forces $\lambda\unrhd
u$: for a component $k$ and row cutoff $r$, labels of type components below $k$ cannot occupy physical components at least $k$, labels of type component $k$ with row at most $r$ cannot occupy physical components greater than $k$ and occupy at most $r$ nodes per column of physical component $k$ by strict column increase, so the count $\sum_{a<k}|
u^{(a)}|+\sum_{i\le r}
u^{(k)}_i$ is at most $\sum_{a<k}|\lambda^{(a)}|+\sum_{i\le r}\lambda^{(k)}_i$, which is exactly the multipartition dominance inequality; and $T^\lambda$ is the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, so the Kostka matrix is unitriangular. [F1, F2, F6, algebra]

The standard basis of $G_0$ and block purity. The matrix of standard multiplicities is unitriangular with diagonal $1$ by step 1.2, so inverting it by backward substitution shows that the classes $[\Delta_\lambda]$ form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(C_n\text{-mod})$ ([F5]). Projecting to blocks is exact. Every $\Delta_\lambda$ is nonzero and block-pure by [F3], so if a class supported in one block equals $\sum_\lambda a_\lambda[\Delta_\lambda]$, then every coefficient of a standard lying in another block vanishes by this basis independence; this is the block-separation input used by the Jantzen equivalence. [F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

The corner functor and the radical comparison. Put $e=e_\omega$; then $eCe\cong H_n$ by step 1.1, and $V\mapsto Ve$ is exact. Semistandard tableaux of type $\omega$ are canonically standard multitableaux: replacing the label $(r,\ell)$ by $r$ is a bijection onto the standard tableaux, and the surviving standard vectors $v_t$ of $\Delta_\lambda e$ carry the same right-$H_n$ action as the Murphy vectors $m_t$ of $S_\lambda$ by the cell multiplication [F2]; this is an explicit isomorphism $\Delta_\lambda e\cong S_\lambda$. The forms also agree: in $C_n$, $\langle v_s,v_t\rangle e_\lambda\equiv\varphi_{(T^\lambda,s)}\varphi_{(t,T^\lambda)}$ modulo higher $C_n$-shapes, and evaluating the two factors at $m_\lambda$ gives the product $m_{(t^\lambda,s)}m_{(t,t^\lambda)}$, whose coefficient of $m_\lambda$ modulo higher $H_n$-shapes is exactly the Specht form entry; a higher Schur map evaluates to a sum of higher Murphy shapes by its explicit definition, so no shape error is lost. Since $e^*=e$, the $e$ and $1-e$ parts of $\Delta_\lambda$ are orthogonal: if $x$ pairs to zero against $\Delta_\lambda e$, then $\langle x,y(1-e)\rangle=\langle x(1-e),y\rangle=0$, so $\mathrm{rad}(\Delta_\lambda)e=\mathrm{rad}(\Delta_\lambda)\cap\Delta_\lambda e=\mathrm{rad}(\Delta_\lambda e)$. Hence $L_\lambda e\cong D_\lambda$ for every $\lambda$, with $D_\lambda$ allowed to be zero. Applying the exact functor to a composition series of $\Delta_\lambda$, each simple factor $L_\mu$ becomes $D_\mu$ or $0$, and the nonzero $D_\mu$ are pairwise distinct and exhaustive by [F3]; hence $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]=[S_\lambda:D_\mu]$ for every $\mu$ with $D_\mu\ne0$, with no simple-label bijection through $e$ assumed. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

Typed Schur/Specht block linkage. The center isomorphism of step 1.1 sends a central block idempotent $b$ of $H_n$ to the same right-action projection on $M$, hence to the corresponding central idempotent $b_{C}$ of $C_n$, and on the corner $Vb_Ce=(Ve)b$. Every $\Delta_\lambda$ is nonzero and block-pure by [F3], and $\Delta_\lambda e\cong S_\lambda$ is nonzero because $S_\lambda$ has its Murphy standard-tableau basis; consequently the block supporting $\Delta_\lambda$ corresponds to exactly the block supporting $S_\lambda$. Therefore $\Delta_\lambda,\Delta_\mu$ share a $C_n$-block if and only if $S_\lambda,S_\mu$ share an $H_n$-block, and [F3] describes both sides as linkage by chains of cell modules with neighbouring terms sharing a simple composition factor; step 2.2 supplies the multiplicity transfers when a nonzero simple is needed. No equality-of-residue-contents assertion is used. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

Assign to each standard multitableau the sequence of joint Jucys–Murphy words: the diagonal values $U_az^{j-i}$ at the nodes carrying the labels $1,\dots,n$ ([F3]). If two standard multitableaux first differ at step $r$, then their restrictions to the boxes $1,\dots,r-1$ coincide, and the two added nodes are two different addable nodes of that common prefix shape. If the two nodes lie in one physical component, their contents $j-i$ are different (two addable nodes of a partition have different contents), and $z$ is transcendental over the base field, so $z^{j-i}\ne z^{j'-i'}$. If they lie in different components $a\ne b$, the values $U_az^{j-i}$ and $U_bz^{j'-i'}$ are distinct in $K$, because $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ are algebraically independent monomials and the components differ. Hence the joint word determines the tableau, different standard multitableaux -- even of different shapes -- have different joint words, and distinct shapes have disjoint sets of word characters. [F1, F3, algebra]

Generic simplicity and split semisimplicity. By [F3] each $S_\lambda$ has a simultaneous triangular filtration whose successive characters are its own words of step 1.1. Hence every composition factor $D_\mu$ of the nonzero module $S_\lambda$ has a word occurring in $S_\mu$ and a word occurring in $S_\lambda$; disjointness of shape word sets forces $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $D_\lambda\ne0$, and the cellular diagonal multiplicity $[S_\lambda:D_\lambda]=1$ of [F4] forces $S_\lambda=D_\lambda$ to be simple, with the distinct absolutely simple modules $S_\lambda$ as the only composition factors. The cellular basis gives $\dim_K H_K=\sum_\lambda(\dim_K S_\lambda)^2$. The semisimple quotient is a product of full matrix algebras on the exhaustive absolutely simple $S_\lambda$: to see this, the rank-one cell action on each simple gives every matrix unit, and the distinct simple labels give the distinct simple factors. Its dimension is the same sum, so the radical has dimension zero. Thus $H_K$ is split semisimple; no splitting of the cellular filtration was assumed. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

Word separation for the Lyle–Mathas deformation. Fix $N\ge1$, nonzero $q_H,Q_a$ in $F$, and set $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{Na}$ in $F(t)$. For two standard multitableaux that first differ at a step $r\le N$, the common prefix of size $r-1$ has components of sizes summing to $r-1$; the two added nodes lie in components $a,b$ and each added content $c=j-i$ is bounded in absolute value by the size of its own component, so $|c-c'|<r\le N$. A collision $U_az^c=U_bz^{c'}$ with $a\ne b$ would force the equality $Na+c=Nb+c'$ of $t$-adic exponents, i.e. the nonzero multiple $N(a-b)$ of $N$ would equal $c'-c$ with $|c'-c|<N$, impossible. If $a=b$, then $z$ is transcendental over $F$, so $z^c=z^{c'}$ forces $c=c'$. Thus the joint words separate all rank-$d$ standards in $F(t)$ as in step 1.1, and the argument of step 2.1 proves that the rank-$d$ Specht modules are simple and the corresponding Hecke algebra is split semisimple over $F(t)$, with no affine-center or block-classification input. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

Nondegenerate Schur standards. By [F6], over any field with unit parameters, $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]=[S_\lambda:D_\mu]$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$, and every $\Delta_\lambda$ is nonzero. Over $K$, step 2.1 makes every $S_\lambda$ simple; hence $D_\mu=0$ never occurs, $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\lambda]=[S_\lambda:S_\lambda]=1$, and since all $L_\mu$ are distinct the multiplicity list forces $\Delta_\lambda=L_\lambda$ to be simple; the diagonal cell-form entry of the standard of shape and type $\lambda$ is $1$, so the cellular form is nonzero and, being invariant on a simple module, is nondegenerate. The same argument applies over $F(t)$ to the rank-$d$ standards using step 3.1, and the construction of [F5] and the multiplicities of [F6] are identities over the respective ground fields, so the charged finite-$e$ specializations used by the Lyle–Mathas deformation are included. No valuation of a weight-Gram determinant is computed. [F5, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

Let $R:=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ be the universal
Laurent parameter ring of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], and let
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the $R$-algebra presented there by the commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$, the generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the quadratic, braid,
distant, Bernstein and mixed-commutation relations — **without** imposing the
first-variable cyclotomic relation. Then:

1. both families
   $$X^aT_w\quad\text{and}\quad T_wX^a\qquad(a\in\mathbb Z^n,\ w\in S_n)$$
   are $R$-bases of $H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$, and the same two families are bases
   after arbitrary base change to a commutative ring in which $z$ is a unit;
2. left multiplication by any nonzero element of the Laurent polynomial
   subalgebra $R[X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_n^{\pm1}]\subseteq H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ is
   injective;
3. after localizing at the differences $X_i-X_j$ ($i\ne j$), the algebra maps
   into the rational crossed product of the fraction field of the polynomial
   ring with $S_n$, and in that localization the elements
   $$\Phi_i:=T_i-\frac{(z-1)X_{i+1}}{X_{i+1}-X_i} =T_i-c_{i,i+1},\qquad c_{ij}:=\frac{(z-1)X_j}{X_j-X_i},$$
   satisfy $\Phi_if=s_i(f)\Phi_i$ for every (localized) Laurent polynomial $f$.

No cyclotomic basis, Brundan–Kleshchev theorem, trace form or
primitive-content assertion is used.

For $H_n$ in
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all
$\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a
basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$
with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$ independent of $s$. The higher spans are
actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters
inherits the cellular basis; in particular the arbitrary-field finite-$e$
charged specializations and the LM deformation DVR retain it. The universal
rank is supplied independently by
[[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], not by a
primitive-block classification.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

Let $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ be the arbitrary-level cyclotomic Hecke
algebra of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]]
over a commutative ring $R$ in which $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ are units, and let
$\mu$ be an $\ell$-multipartition of $n$. Then the submodule
$M_\mu=m_\mu H_n\subseteq H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard multitableaux of multipartition shape
$\lambda$ and type $\mu$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of shape $\lambda$,
with $\mu(s)$ the row-and-component reading. The sums have disjoint
coefficient-$1$ Murphy pivots, so they are $R$-independent and $M_\mu$ is a
direct summand of $H_n$ as an $R$-module. The statement holds first over the
universal Laurent parameter ring and then over every commutative
specialization with unit parameters: the proof constructs, for each $(S,t)$,
an explicit affine element $h$ with $m_{(S,t)}=m_\mu h$ and uses no
quantum-factorial or parameter-difference division, and the equality descends
to $R$ by coefficient identities rather than by generic flatness. The Specht
filtration of $M_\mu$ is ordered by higher shapes and contains one copy of the
Specht module $S_\lambda$ for each semistandard $S$, and no primitive-block
classification is used.

For $H_n$, the summands $M_\lambda=m_\lambda H_n$, the direct sum
$M=\bigoplus_\lambda M_\lambda$ and the multipartition-summand algebra
$C_n=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M)$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]],
evaluation $f\mapsto f(m_\nu)$ identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(M_\nu,M_\mu)\cong M_\mu\cap H_nm_\nu,$$
with $R$-basis the rectangular sums $m_{(S,T)}$ over $S$ semistandard of
shape $\lambda$ and type $\mu$ and $T$ semistandard of shape $\lambda$ and
type $\nu$. Consequently the maps $\varphi_{ST}$ are actual well-defined
endomorphisms of $M$ and form a free dominance-cellular basis of $C_n$ with
$\varphi_{ST}^*=\varphi_{TS}$ and
$$\varphi_{ST}\varphi\equiv\sum_W r_{(T,W)}(\varphi)\,\varphi_{SW}\pmod{C_n^{\rhd\lambda}}$$
with coefficients independent of $S$. The formation of this basis and its
constants specializes to every commutative unit-parameter base, including the
LM deformation DVR. The proof uses the perfect symmetric canonical trace
([[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-canonical-trace-is-perfect-and-symmetric]])
and the codomain direct-summand pivots
([[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-row-type-sums-give-permutation-module-bases]]);
no field-only double-annihilator and no nonsaturated-lattice argument is used.

Over the fraction field of the universal Laurent parameter ring, all
cyclotomic Specht modules are simple and $H_n$ is split semisimple; all Schur
standards $\Delta_\lambda$ equal $L_\lambda$ and have nondegenerate cellular
forms. Moreover, fix $N\ge1$, a field $F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$,
and $0\le d\le N$, and take
$\mathcal O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)}$ with $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{Na}$. Over $F(t)$,
all rank-$d$ Specht and Schur standards are simple and their forms are
nondegenerate. This includes the charged finite-$e$ specialization used by
the Lyle–Mathas deformation. The lemma establishes generic nondegeneracy only;
it does not prove any signed-rim-hook weight-Gram determinant valuation
formula.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is
$$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$
The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

When $A$ is real, $|\det A|$ means the ordinary real absolute value of its real determinant. It is not alternate notation for the determinant itself.

For $n\ge1$ and $A,B\in M_n(R)$ over a commutative ring,
$$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B).$$

For every $n\ge1$, every commutative ring $R$, and every $A\in M_n(R)$,
$$\det(A^{\mathsf T})=\det(A).$$

e1}b_w(X)\Phi_w$ and using that every $\Phi_w$ with $w
