citations.quote:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

Let $R:=\mathbb Z[z^{\pm1},U_1^{\pm1},\dots,U_\ell^{\pm1}]$ be the universal
Laurent parameter ring of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], and let
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the $R$-algebra presented there by the commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$, the generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the quadratic, braid,
distant, Bernstein and mixed-commutation relations — **without** imposing the
first-variable cyclotomic relation. Then:

1. both families
   $$X^aT_w\quad\text{and}\quad T_wX^a\qquad(a\in\mathbb Z^n,\ w\in S_n)$$
   are $R$-bases of $H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$, and the same two families are bases
   after arbitrary base change to a commutative ring in which $z$ is a unit;
2. left multiplication by any nonzero element of the Laurent polynomial
   subalgebra $R[X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_n^{\pm1}]\subseteq H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ is
   injective;
3. after localizing at the differences $X_i-X_j$ ($i\ne j$), the algebra maps
   into the rational crossed product of the fraction field of the polynomial
   ring with $S_n$, and in that localization the elements
   $$\Phi_i:=T_i-\frac{(z-1)X_{i+1}}{X_{i+1}-X_i} =T_i-c_{i,i+1},\qquad c_{ij}:=\frac{(z-1)X_j}{X_j-X_i},$$
   satisfy $\Phi_if=s_i(f)\Phi_i$ for every (localized) Laurent polynomial $f$.

No cyclotomic basis, Brundan–Kleshchev theorem, trace form or
primitive-content assertion is used.

For $H_n$ in
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all
$\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a
basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$
with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$ independent of $s$. The higher spans are
actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters
inherits the cellular basis; in particular the arbitrary-field finite-$e$
charged specializations and the LM deformation DVR retain it. The universal
rank is supplied independently by
[[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], not by a
primitive-block classification.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

Let $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ be the arbitrary-level cyclotomic Hecke
algebra of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]]
over a commutative ring $R$ in which $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ are units, and let
$\mu$ be an $\ell$-multipartition of $n$. Then the submodule
$M_\mu=m_\mu H_n\subseteq H_n$ has $R$-basis
$$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},$$
where $S$ ranges over the semistandard multitableaux of multipartition shape
$\lambda$ and type $\mu$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of shape $\lambda$,
with $\mu(s)$ the row-and-component reading. The sums have disjoint
coefficient-$1$ Murphy pivots, so they are $R$-independent and $M_\mu$ is a
direct summand of $H_n$ as an $R$-module. The statement holds first over the
universal Laurent parameter ring and then over every commutative
specialization with unit parameters: the proof constructs, for each $(S,t)$,
an explicit affine element $h$ with $m_{(S,t)}=m_\mu h$ and uses no
quantum-factorial or parameter-difference division, and the equality descends
to $R$ by coefficient identities rather than by generic flatness. The Specht
filtration of $M_\mu$ is ordered by higher shapes and contains one copy of the
Specht module $S_\lambda$ for each semistandard $S$, and no primitive-block
classification is used.

For $H_n$, the summands $M_\lambda=m_\lambda H_n$, the direct sum
$M=\bigoplus_\lambda M_\lambda$ and the multipartition-summand algebra
$C_n=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M)$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]],
evaluation $f\mapsto f(m_\nu)$ identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(M_\nu,M_\mu)\cong M_\mu\cap H_nm_\nu,$$
with $R$-basis the rectangular sums $m_{(S,T)}$ over $S$ semistandard of
shape $\lambda$ and type $\mu$ and $T$ semistandard of shape $\lambda$ and
type $\nu$. Consequently the maps $\varphi_{ST}$ are actual well-defined
endomorphisms of $M$ and form a free dominance-cellular basis of $C_n$ with
$\varphi_{ST}^*=\varphi_{TS}$ and
$$\varphi_{ST}\varphi\equiv\sum_W r_{(T,W)}(\varphi)\,\varphi_{SW}\pmod{C_n^{\rhd\lambda}}$$
with coefficients independent of $S$. The formation of this basis and its
constants specializes to every commutative unit-parameter base, including the
LM deformation DVR. The proof uses the perfect symmetric canonical trace
([[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-canonical-trace-is-perfect-and-symmetric]])
and the codomain direct-summand pivots
([[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-row-type-sums-give-permutation-module-bases]]);
no field-only double-annihilator and no nonsaturated-lattice argument is used.

Over the fraction field of the universal Laurent parameter ring, all
cyclotomic Specht modules are simple and $H_n$ is split semisimple; all Schur
standards $\Delta_\lambda$ equal $L_\lambda$ and have nondegenerate cellular
forms. Moreover, fix $N\ge1$, a field $F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$,
and $0\le d\le N$, and take
$\mathcal O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)}$ with $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{Na}$. Over $F(t)$,
all rank-$d$ Specht and Schur standards are simple and their forms are
nondegenerate. This includes the charged finite-$e$ specialization used by
the Lyle–Mathas deformation. The lemma establishes generic nondegeneracy only;
it does not prove any signed-rim-hook weight-Gram determinant valuation
formula.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is
$$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$
The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

When $A$ is real, $|\det A|$ means the ordinary real absolute value of its real determinant. It is not alternate notation for the determinant itself.

For $n\ge1$ and $A,B\in M_n(R)$ over a commutative ring,
$$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B).$$

For every $n\ge1$, every commutative ring $R$, and every $A\in M_n(R)$,
$$\det(A^{\mathsf T})=\det(A).$$

citations.quote:
Work with the arbitrary-level Murphy/Schur datum of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
either (i) the fraction field $K$ of the universal Laurent parameter ring,
including the generic field of the Lyle–Mathas deformation, or (ii) any field
$F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$ under the deformation
$z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$ in $F(t)$. Let $b_\lambda$ be the Murphy cellular
form on the Specht module $V_\lambda$ with basis $v_s$ over standard
tableaux $s$ and $v_0=v_{t^\lambda}$; put
$B_k=\sum_{a\le k}|\nu^{(a)}|$,
$u_\nu=\prod_{k=2}^{\ell}\prod_{r=1}^{B_{k-1}}(X_r-U_k)$,
$x_\nu=\sum_{w\in\mathfrak S_\nu}T_w$, $m_\nu=u_\nu x_\nu$, let $A_\nu$ be
the action of $m_\nu$ on $V_\lambda$, let
$P_\nu(z)=\sum_{w\in\mathfrak S_\nu}z^{\ell(w)}$, and let
$$f_s=v_s+\sum_{r\triangleright s}a_{sr}v_r,\qquad \gamma_s=b_\lambda(f_s,f_s)$$
be the monic simultaneous Jucys–Murphy eigenbasis and its norms. Let
$G_{\lambda\nu}$ be the Schur cellular Gram matrix on the type-$\nu$ basis of
$\Delta(\lambda)$, indexed by the semistandard $T$ of shape $\lambda$ and type
$\nu$, and for such $T$ let $t_T$ be its dominance-minimal standard
refinement, $r_x=U_{a(x)}z^{\operatorname{content}(x)}$ the residue of the node
$x$ of $\lambda$, and $a_T(x)$ the type component of the label of $x$. Then
$$\det G_{\lambda\nu}=\prod_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)}\frac{\gamma_{t_T}}{C_{t_T}\,u_T},\qquad C_t=\prod_{i<j\ \mathrm{same\ type\ row}}\frac{z\,r_t(j)-r_t(i)}{r_t(j)-r_t(i)},\qquad u_T=\prod_x\prod_{b>a_T(x)}(r_x-U_b),$$
with empty determinant $1$. The monic transition determinant from the
semistandard basis $(w_T)$ to the chain basis $(g_T)$ is exactly $1$.
Equivalently, with $C(A,B)=\frac{zB-A}{B-A}$,
$R(A,B)=\frac{(zB-A)(B-zA)}{(B-A)^2}$ and
$\mathcal C(T),\mathcal I(T)$ the pair lists of the proof,
$$\det G_{\lambda\nu}=\prod_TB_T\prod_{x<y}C(r_x,r_y)^{c_{xy}}R(r_x,r_y)^{i_{xy}},\qquad B_T=\prod_x\prod_{a(x)<b\le a_T(x)}(r_x-U_b),$$
where $c_{xy},i_{xy}$ are explicit nonnegative semistandard counts. All
factors are nonzero in the stated generic fields, and no quantum factorial is
inverted in the $\mathcal O$-lattice; arbitrary composition series are
auxiliary only.

Let $F$ be a field, let $F[t,t^{-1}]$ be its Laurent polynomial ring
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and let $v_1$ be the $(t-1)$-adic
valuation on the nonzero elements of $F[t,t^{-1}]$: for $0\ne f$,
$$v_1(f):=\max\{n\ge0:(t-1)^n\mid f\ \text{in}\ F[t,t^{-1}]\},$$
so that $v_1(f)=0$ exactly when $f(1)\ne0$
([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]). Let $A,B\in F\setminus\{0\}$, let $u,v\in\mathbb Z$,
put $N:=u-v$ and $f:=At^u-Bt^v$.

1. If $A\ne B$, then $v_1(f)=0$.
2. If $A=B$ and $N\ne0$, then $v_1(f)=1$ when $\operatorname{char}F=0$, and
   $v_1(f)=p^{v_p(|N|)}$ when $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$; here $v_p$ is the
   exponent of $p$ in $|N|$, i.e. $N=p^r m$ with $p\nmid m$
   ([[def-ring-characteristic]]).
3. If $A=B$ and $N=0$, then $f=0$, and the zero element has no finite valuation.

In the intended application the Laurent polynomials $Q_aq_H^{\,j-i}t^{\,na+j-i}$
(foot residues of the Jantzen expression) are compared by this lemma: it
computes their valuation exactly when their difference is nonzero and prevents
replacing valuations by an equality-of-residues indicator in positive
characteristic.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $[\lambda]$ be its Young diagram
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A **tableau of shape
$\lambda$**, or $\lambda$-tableau, is a bijection
$$t:[\lambda]\longrightarrow\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$$
We write $t(i,j)$ for the entry of $t$ in the node $(i,j)$, and we display $t$
as the diagram $[\lambda]$ with each node carrying its entry. Thus a tableau
places each of the numbers $1,\dots,n$ in exactly one node of $[\lambda]$. For
$\lambda=\varnothing$ the diagram is empty and the empty map is the unique
tableau of shape $\varnothing$, the **empty tableau**. The **shape** of a
tableau $t$ is the partition $\lambda$ with $t:[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$,
which is determined by $t$ because $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$.

**Standard tableaux.** A tableau $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is **standard** if its
entries strictly increase along rows and down columns, that is, if
$$t(i,j)<t(i,j+1)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i,j+1)\in[\lambda],$$
$$t(i,j)<t(i+1,j)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i+1,j)\in[\lambda].$$
The empty tableau is standard, because both conditions are vacuous, and it is
the unique standard tableau of shape $\varnothing$. Following the classical
notation we write $f^\lambda$ for the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux.

**The left action on tableaux.** For $\sigma\in S_n$ and a $\lambda$-tableau
$t$, define
$$(\sigma\cdot t)(i,j):=\sigma\bigl(t(i,j)\bigr)\qquad\bigl((i,j)\in[\lambda]\bigr).$$
Since $t$ is a bijection onto $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $\sigma$ is a bijection of
$\{1,\dots,n\}$, the map $\sigma\cdot t$ is again a bijection
$[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$, hence again a $\lambda$-tableau, and
$\mathrm{id}\cdot t=t$, $\sigma\cdot(\tau\cdot t)=(\sigma\tau)\cdot t$ for all
$\sigma,\tau\in S_n$: the rule is a left action of $S_n$ on the set of
$\lambda$-tableaux. For every $\sigma\in S_n$ the row sets of $\sigma\cdot t$
are the images under $\sigma$ of the row sets of $t$, and the column sets of
$\sigma\cdot t$ are the images under $\sigma$ of the column sets of $t$.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and $\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$,
with diagrams $[\lambda]$ and $[\mu]$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). For content counts
only, set $\mu_i:=0$ for $i$ beyond the number of parts of $\mu$; these
zeros are not additional parts of the partition.

A **semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$ and content $\mu$**, also called a
semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$ and **type $\mu$**, is a filling
$T:[\lambda]\to\{1,2,\dots\}$ of the boxes of $[\lambda]$ with positive
integers such that:

1. **content:** for every $i\ge 1$ the entry $i$ occurs in exactly $\mu_i$
   boxes of $[\lambda]$, so the multiset of entries is
   $\{1^{\mu_1},2^{\mu_2},\dots\}$ and in particular every entry lies between
   $1$ and the number of parts of $\mu$;
2. **rows:** the entries weakly increase along every row, that is,
   $T(i,j)\le T(i,j+1)$ whenever $(i,j)$ and $(i,j+1)$ are both in
   $[\lambda]$;
3. **columns:** the entries strictly increase down every column, that is,
   $T(i,j)<T(i+1,j)$ whenever $(i,j)$ and $(i+1,j)$ are both in $[\lambda]$.

The **Kostka number** $K_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the number of semistandard
tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and content $\mu$:
$$K_{\lambda,\mu}:=\#\{\,T:T\text{ is a semistandard }\lambda\text{-tableau of content }\mu\,\}.$$
This is well defined and finite: a filling of the $n$ boxes of $[\lambda]$ by
positive integers has at most $n^n$ possibilities for $n\ge1$ once each entry is required
to lie between $1$ and the number of parts of $\mu$, and conditions 1--3 cut this
finite set down to the semistandard tableaux, so $K_{\lambda,\mu}$ is a
nonnegative integer. It is zero when the conditions cannot be met.

Two entries may be equal inside a row, but never inside a column: a repeated
entry in a column would contradict the strict increase of condition 3, so the
repetitions of a label forced by the content $\mu$ must be spread across
distinct columns of $[\lambda]$. For $\lambda=\mu=\varnothing$ there is a
single filling, the empty one, so
$$K_{\varnothing,\varnothing}=1 .$$

**Relation to standard tableaux.** Because a tableau of content $(1^n)$ uses
each of the numbers $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, its entries are pairwise
distinct, and weak increase along a row is then strict increase along that
row; a filling of $[\lambda]$ with content $(1^n)$ is therefore semistandard
exactly when it is a standard $\lambda$-tableau
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]), that is,
$$K_{\lambda,(1^n)}=f^\lambda ,$$
the number of standard tableaux of shape $\lambda$. In particular, for $n\ge1$,
$K_{(n),(1^n)}=K_{(n),(n)}=1$, since the single row carries either the
standard entries $1,2,\dots,n$ or the $n$ copies of the entry $1$, and
$K_{(1^n),(1^n)}=1$, realized by the single column $1,2,\dots,n$ read from
top to bottom.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is
$$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$
The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

When $A$ is real, $|\det A|$ means the ordinary real absolute value of its real determinant. It is not alternate notation for the determinant itself.

derivations.claim: Characters as finite symmetric polynomials. Fix $d\ge n$ row labels per type component with ordered variables $x_{(a,r)}$, put $Y_a=\{x_{(b,r)}:b\ge a\}$ with the inherited order, and for a shape $\lambda$ let $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}(\lambda)}x^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$. The flag condition says that the physical component $a$ of a semistandard tableau is an ordinary semistandard tableau over the alphabet $Y_a$, and the components are chosen independently, so $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\prod_a s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $s_\rho(Y)=\det(h_{\rho_i-i+j}(Y))$. The determinant equals the ordinary semistandard generating polynomial: expand it as signed families of east/north lattice paths from $(-j,1)$ to $(\rho_i-i,m)$ with east steps at height $r$ weighted $y_r$, choose the first intersection in a fixed order and exchange the two tails, an involution that preserves the monomial weight and reverses the permutation sign, so all intersecting families cancel; a nonintersecting family forces the identity matching, and the surviving families are exactly the semistandard tableaux, sign $+1$. Hence the coefficient of $x^\nu$ in $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda$ is the Kostka number $K_{\lambda\nu}$; empty and short-row cases are included.

Beta determinants and rim-hook signs. Choose $N\ge n$, put $\beta_{a,i}=\lambda^{(a)}_i+N-i$ with zero parts appended, and for a nonnegative integer array $v$ define $\chi(v;x)=\prod_a\det\bigl(h_{v_{a,i}-N+j}(Y_a)\bigr)_{i,j}$. If two entries of one component of $v$ agree the determinant has equal rows and is zero; otherwise sorting that component into strictly decreasing order and writing $\rho_i=v'_i-N+i$ gives $\chi(v;x)=\varepsilon(v)\prod_a s_{\rho^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $\varepsilon$ the product of the row-sorting signs, so every coefficient is a signed Kostka multiplicity. A beta move lowering a bead from $v+L$ to an unoccupied $v$ is exactly the removal of a rim hook of length $L$: tracing the southeast boundary shows the strip between the two boundary steps has $L$ boxes, its leg is the number of occupied positions strictly between $v$ and $v+L$, its foot content is $v-N+1$, and the associated sorting sign is $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$; the correspondence is a bijection by the reverse move.

The hook side as a complete finite alternating polynomial. Define $B_\lambda(x)$ as the finite alternating sum of step 2.1: for crosscomponent terms, over $a<b$, over beads $i,j$ and lengths $h\le\beta_{a,i}$, of $\chi(\beta-h e_{a,i}+h e_{b,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_bz^{\beta_{b,j}})$; and for same-component terms, over $a$, $i<j$ and $1\le h\le\beta_{a,i}-\beta_{a,j}-1$, of $\chi(\beta-he_{a,i}+he_{a,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_az^{\beta_{a,j}})$; terms whose $\chi$ is the zero polynomial are omitted before any valuation is evaluated. Then $B_\lambda(x)=\sum_{\mu:\lambda\triangleright\mu}J_{\lambda\mu}\operatorname{ch}_\mu(x)$: a crosscomponent move removing from the earlier component $a$ and adding to a later component $b>a$ produces a strictly dominated $\mu$ and occurs exactly once by the bead description; occupied targets give repeated rows and zero; sorting contributes $(-1)^{\text{removed leg}+\text{added leg}}$; and the prefactor $z^{-N+1}$ converts the beta difference to the difference of the deformed foot residues. In one component the two moved beads $i<j$ give a strict dominance decrease precisely for $1\le h<\beta_i-\beta_j$, the exchange case $h=\beta_i-\beta_j$ giving $\mu=\lambda$ and the outward case giving the reverse dominance; occupied intermediate positions again give zero rows, and the range exceeding a component's size gives a repeated or negative bead, hence a zero determinant. Thus no hook pair is lost or added, and the surviving summands are exactly the $J_{\lambda\mu}$ terms.

Nonvanishing of every retained foot difference. For a removable rim hook of length $L$ from a partition of size $M+L$ with foot $(h,j)$, one has $-(M+L-1)\le j-h\le M$: every box left of the foot in its row survives, so $j-1\le M$, and $h\le M+L$ gives the lower bound. If $\lambda$ and $\mu$ remove equal-length hooks in distinct components $a\ne b$ to the same remainder with remainder sizes $M_a,M_b$, their foot contents satisfy $|\gamma_x-\gamma_y|\le M_a+M_b+L-1\le n-1$, so the exponent $n(a-b)+\gamma_x-\gamma_y$ is a nonzero integer; in the same component equal foot content and equal length reconstruct the same inverse hook addition, hence would force $\lambda=\mu$, which the strict-dominance terms exclude. Therefore every retained Laurent difference $U_az^u-U_bz^v$ is nonzero in $F(t)$: it is a unit times a nonzero Laurent monomial times $(z^{N}-1)$-type factors and, by [F2], its valuation is finite, being $0$ when the constant residues differ, $1$ in characteristic zero when they agree, and $p^{v_p(N)}$ in characteristic $p$ when they agree.

The same-component operator. In the same-component beta sum put $D=\beta_i-\beta_j$ and $k=D-h$, so the valuation is $f(k)=V(z^k-1)$ up to unit factors; swapping the two changed determinant rows shows $\chi(\beta-(D-k)e_i+(D-k)e_j;x)=-\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$. Hence the complete coefficient of $f(k)$ is $-\sum_{i<j:\beta_i-\beta_j>k}\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$, which is the strictly dominance-lowering part of $-p_kp_k^\perp$ on the abstract shape basis, where $p_k^\perp$ lowers an occupied bead by $k$ into an unoccupied nonnegative position with sign $(-1)^{\#\text{crossed beads}}$ and $p_k$ raises a bead by $k$ with the same sign rule; the bead-raising formula follows from the alternant identity $\det(y_r^{\beta_i})\sum_ry_r^k=\sum_i\det(y_r^{\beta_i+k\delta_{ij}})$ divided by the Vandermonde, and the removal map is its transpose. After one removal and one addition a non-diagonal lower-dominance result comes only from distinct beads $i<j$ with $0<k<\beta_i-\beta_j$, occupied intermediate positions giving zero repeated rows and the diagonal being removed by the strict projection; this proves the operator identification integrally, in every characteristic.

The crosscomponent operator as exterior currents. On the $N$-fold exterior power of a space with basis $e_0,e_1,\dots$, represent a partition by the ordered wedge of its beta beads and let $E(p,q)$ insert $e_p$ after removing $e_q$, with exterior signs; it vanishes if $q$ is absent or $p$ is occupied, and its sign is the bead-sorting sign. Expanding $E=\text{creation}\cdot\text{contraction}$ gives $[E(p,q),E(r,s)]=\delta_{q,r}E(p,s)-\delta_{p,s}E(r,q)$. The crosscomponent matrix acting on column shape vectors is $J^{\mathrm{cross}}=\sum_{a<b}\sum_{h>0}\sum_{q\ge h,w\ge0}V(U_az^{q-h}-U_bz^w)E_a(q,q-h)E_b(w,w+h)$, a finite operator on each size-$n$ sector; the reverse hook pair has forward current $E_a(q-h,q)E_b(w+h,w)$, and transposing gives exactly this operator with the same signs and valuation.

Horizontal strips and their conjugation. With $S e_q=e_{q+1}$ and $H(x)=(I-xS)^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge0}x^rS^r$, whose entry $H_{p,q}$ is $x^{p-q}$ for $p\ge q$ and $0$ otherwise, the matrix of $\wedge^NH(x)$ between $\beta_\mu$ and $\beta_\rho$ is $x^{|\mu|-|\rho|}\det(1_{\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,j}})$. Subtracting consecutive columns of the $0/1$ matrix makes its determinant $1$ exactly when $\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,i}>\beta_{\mu,i+1}$ for all $i$, i.e. $\mu_i\ge\rho_i\ge\mu_{i+1}$, the horizontal-strip criterion, and $0$ otherwise; so $\Gamma(x)=\wedge^NH(x)$ adds every horizontal strip once with weight $x^{\text{strip size}}$. For a type component $a$, $\Gamma_a(x)=\prod_{b\le a}\Gamma_b(x)$ adds a horizontal strip in every permitted physical component $b\le a$ and leaves the rest unchanged, so the successive $\Gamma_a$ from the empty shape enumerate exactly the flagged semistandard tableaux and give the branching matrix. Conjugation is explicit: since $H^{-1}=I-xS$ has column vector $e_p-xe_{p+1}$ and row covector $\sum_{r\le q}x^{q-r}e_r^*$, $\Gamma(x)^{-1}E(p,q)\Gamma(x)=\sum_{r=0}^qx^{q-r}\bigl(E(p,r)-xE(p+1,r)\bigr),$ and the two-current conjugation is the ordered product of two such sums.

Strip factors and exact minor expressions. For a permitted strip transition $\rho\to\lambda$ for the next type component $c$, let $\eta=[\lambda]\setminus[\rho]$, $r_x=U_{\operatorname{comp}(x)}z^{\operatorname{content}(x)}$, and put $F^{(c)}_{\lambda\rho}=\prod_{x\in\eta}\prod_{\operatorname{comp}(x)<b\le c}(r_x-U_b)\prod_{x\in[\rho],\,y\in\eta\text{ in one physical row}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{x<y,\,x,y\in\eta\text{ in different physical rows}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{x\in\eta,\,y\in[\rho],\,x<y}R(r_x,r_y)$. Splitting the pair lists of [F1] into old/old, old/new and new/new gives this factor, and their product along a semistandard chain is $\gamma_{t_T}/(C_{t_T}u_T)$. Choose $N>n$, write $q_i=\beta_{\lambda,i}$, $p_i=\beta_{\rho,i}$ in each component, and $H(q,p)_{ij}=1_{q_i\ge p_j}$, so $q_N=p_N=0$. Write $\phi(k)=V(z^k-1)$ for $k>0$ and $\psi_{ab}(d)=V(U_az^d-U_b)$. First regard these as independent formal symbols; canceled symbols are never evaluated. By steps 3.1 and 5.1, the same-component row contribution to $J\Gamma$ is $\sum_{i<j}\sum_{0<h<q_i-q_j}\phi(q_i-q_j-h)\det H(q-he_i+he_j,p)$; the column contribution to $\Gamma J$ is $\sum_{i<j}\sum_{h>0}(\phi(p_i-p_j+h)-\phi(h))\det H(q,p+he_i-he_j)$. Negative or repeated shifted beads give zero determinants. For the second formula, the outward source has beads $p_i+h,p_j-h$; its two hook pairs returning to $p$ have lengths $h$ and $p_i-p_j+h$, foot gaps $p_i-p_j+h$ and $h$, and opposite signs because the second pair exchanges the two target beads. This proves the difference of potentials, including crossed inverse sources. A crosscomponent row term replaces $q_{a,i},q_{b,j}$ by $q_{a,i}-h,q_{b,j}+h$ with potential $\psi_{ab}(q_{a,i}-h-q_{b,j})$; its column term replaces $p_{a,i},p_{b,j}$ by $p_{a,i}+h,p_{b,j}-h$ with potential $\psi_{ab}(p_{a,i}-p_{b,j}+h)$. The determinants in the original indexed positions retain all sorting signs.

Norm endpoints. On support $q_i\ge p_i>q_{i+1}$. Put $M_i=q_i-p_i$, $K_j=p_j-q_{j+1}-1$ for $j<N$, $K_N=0$, and $S(m)=\sum_{k=1}^m\phi(k)$. The same-component norm valuation is $\sum_i(S(q_i)-S(p_i)-S(M_i))+\sum_{i<j}\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_j)-\phi(u-p_j+1))$. To verify this directly, put $b_i=N-i$: same-row old/new pairs sum to $S(q_i-b_i)-S(M_i)-S(p_i-b_i)$. For $i<j$, new/new and new-upper/old-lower pairs sum to $\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_j)-\phi(u-p_j+1)+\phi(u-b_j+1)-\phi(u-b_j))$. The last two terms telescope in $u$ to $\phi(q_i-b_j)-\phi(p_i-b_j)$; summing over $j>i$ cancels the baseline $b_i$ terms and gives the formula. Every displayed $\phi$ argument is positive. For $a<b\le c$, the crosscomponent endpoint expression is $\sum_i\sum_{u=p_{a,i}}^{q_{a,i}-1}(\psi_{ab}(u+1)+\sum_{j=1}^N(\psi_{ab}(u-q_{b,j})-\psi_{ab}(u-p_{b,j}+1)))$. Indeed the new/new $C_+$ factors telescope in the lower-component node index $v$ to $\psi(u-q_{b,j})-\psi(u-p_{b,j})$, and the new/old $R$ factors add $\psi(u-p_{b,j})-\psi(u-b_j)$ and the rectangle difference $\sum_{v=b_j}^{p_{b,j}-1}(\psi(u+1-v)-\psi(u-v))$. Telescoping this rectangle in the other direction and adding the boundary factor $\psi(u-N+1)$ gives the displayed formula; the vacuum differences telescope and cancel that boundary. This padded formula is an equality of formal symbols: its $j=N$ term cancels $\psi(u+1)$ before evaluation.

All on-support minors. Here $H$ is the unit upper triangular step matrix. Expanding a replacement row or column in its basis gives $d_i^{\mathrm{row}}(v)=1_{p_i\le v<p_{i-1}}$ and $d_i^{\mathrm{col}}(v)=1_{q_{i+1}<v\le q_i}$, with $p_0=\infty$ and no positive lowering from $p_N=0$. A two-row minor is its direct product minus its crossed product. For the same-component row expression, the direct term has $1\le h\le\min(M_i,K_{j-1})$ and the crossed term, with $k=q_i-q_j-h$, has $1\le k\le\min(M_i,K_{j-1})$. The outward two-column minor has no crossed term and its direct bound is $1\le h\le\min(M_i,K_j)$. Pair direct row index $j+1$ with first-potential column index $j$. For arbitrary symbols $\psi$ the interval identity $\sum_{s=0}^{M-1}(\psi(A+s+K+1)-\psi(A+s+1))=\sum_{h=1}^{\min(M,K)}(\psi(A+M+K+1-h)-\psi(A+h))$ follows by canceling the overlap of the two integer intervals (when $M\le K$ they are disjoint, and when $M>K$ only $K$ endpoints remain). Applying it with $A=p_i-p_j$, the paired contribution is $\sum_{j=i+1}^{N-1}\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}(\phi(u-q_{j+1})-\phi(u-p_j+1))$. Crossed rows cancel the second column potentials except $-S(\min(M_i,K_i))$; the unpaired direct row $j=i+1$, combined with that residual by the same identity at $A=0$, gives $\sum_{u=p_i}^{q_i-1}\phi(u-q_{i+1})-S(M_i)$. Summing yields exactly the same-component endpoints of step 7.1. For a crosscomponent pair, row $j+1$ and column $j$ share the bound $\min(M_i,K_{b,j})$ and $A=p_{a,i}-p_{b,j}$. The unpaired first row contributes $\sum_{u=p_{a,i}}^{q_{a,i}-1}\psi(u-q_{b,1})$; the final column vanishes. The same interval identity converts the paired terms to the remaining endpoints of step 7.1. Thus $(J\Gamma-\Gamma J)_{\lambda\rho}=x^{|\lambda|-|\rho|}V(F^{(c)}_{\lambda\rho})$ on support.

Crosscomponent off support. The row of $H$ at bead $v$ is the tail vector starting at threshold $\kappa(v)$, whose interval is $[p_r,p_{r-1})$. Different nonzero tail vectors are independent; hence rank equals the number of distinct thresholds. At rank $N-1$ there is one missing threshold $r$ and two adjacent duplicated rows $i,i+1$. Put $Q=q_i>Q'=q_{i+1}$, $[P,P')=[p_r,p_{r-1})$, $u=e_i-e_{i+1}$ and $v=e_r-e_{r-1}$, omitting $e_0$. The adjugate is $\varepsilon vu^{\mathsf T}$: its nullspaces have those generators, and removing a duplicate row and the appropriate column gives a minor $\pm1$. Thus replacement determinants are $\varepsilon u_l1_{P\le x<P'}$ and $\varepsilon v_l1_{Q'<x\le Q}$ with the same sign. Rank $\le N-2$ kills every one-row/column replacement. A defective earlier component can be repaired only when $Q'\ge P'$ (missing below), and a defective later component only when $Q<P$ (missing above); opposite directions give zero. If only the earlier component is defective, pair normal later row $j+1$ and column $j$ and write $L=q_{b,j+1}$, $M=p_{b,j}$. Their coefficients both give $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in[P-L,P'-L)\cap(Q'-M,Q-M]}\psi(d)$; the first unpaired row vanishes because its two source signs sum to zero. If only the later component is defective, write its endpoints $R>R'$, $[S,S')$ and let $M=q_{a,i}-p_{a,i}$. The row coefficient at restored position $w$ is $\varepsilon1_{R'+M<w\le R+M}$ on $[S,S')$, and the column coefficient at $t$ is $\varepsilon1_{S\le t+M<S'}$ on $(R',R]$. The translation $w=t+M$ matches their potentials because $q_{a,i}=p_{a,i}+M$. With both components defective, the row coefficient of $\psi(d)$, divided by $\varepsilon_a\varepsilon_b$, is $(1_{S\le Q-d<S'}-1_{S\le Q'-d<S'})(1_{P\le R+d<P'}-1_{P\le R'+d<P'})$; the column coefficient is $(1_{R'<P-d\le R}-1_{R'<P'-d\le R})(1_{Q'<S+d\le Q}-1_{Q'<S'+d\le Q})$. They agree by the endpoint identity $1_{B_0\le A_1-d<B_1}-1_{B_0\le A_0-d<B_1}=1_{A_0<B_0+d\le A_1}-1_{A_0<B_1+d\le A_1}$, obtained by regrouping four half-line indicators. Infinite top endpoints simply omit the virtual source. An untouched defective component kills the product. Components beyond $c$ are empty in the reachable prefix: the forward transfer would create a nonempty forbidden intermediate component, and the inverse transfer would remove a hook from an empty component, so both vanish. This exhausts crosscomponent off-support cases.

Same-component deficiency one, missing below. Keep the rank-one data of step 9.1, with duplicated rows $s,s+1$ and missing threshold $r>s$, so $Q'\ge P'$. A nonzero inward two-row replacement must use one duplicate source and a unique normal row $j\ge r+1$: one new row fills the missing interval and the other restores the unique source threshold. The direct and exchanged assignments have signs $\varepsilon u_l$ and $-\varepsilon u_l$; any other assignment leaves an unchanged duplicate or missing threshold, or violates the strict inward range. Nonzero outward two-column repairs use one endpoint $P,P'$ and a unique column $j\ge r+1$, or the endpoint pair itself. Put $K_j=p_j-q_{j+1}-1$ for $j\ge r$, $K_N=0$. The direct row contribution is $R_j=-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in[P-q_j,P'-q_j)\cap(Q'-p_{j-1},Q-p_{j-1}]}\phi(d)$. Split each unique column contribution into its first and second potentials $C_j^{\mathrm{first}}-C_j^{\mathrm{second}}$ from step 6.1. Then $R_{j+1}=C_j^{\mathrm{first}}$, by the same interval intersection, while $C_j^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{K_j}\phi(h)(1_{Q'<P+h\le Q}-1_{Q'<P'+h\le Q})$. The exchanged row is $X_j=-\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{K_{j-1}}\phi(k)(1_{P\le Q-k<P'}-1_{P\le Q'-k<P'})=-C_{j-1}^{\mathrm{second}}$ by endpoint reciprocity. All terms cancel except $R_{r+1}-C_r^{\mathrm{second}}-C^{\mathrm{end}}$. Put $A=Q'-P'\ge0$, $B=P'-P>0$, $L=Q-Q'>0$, $I_0=(A,A+L]$, $I_1=I_0+B$, $K=K_r$. These three terms are respectively $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap(K,K+B]}\phi(d)$, $\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{K}\phi(h)(1_{I_1}(h)-1_{I_0}(h))$, and $-\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le K}(\phi(B+h)-\phi(h))$; the endpoint-pair sign is negative because the raised endpoint is $P'$. Their residual is $-\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap[1,K+B]}\phi(d)+\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le K}\phi(B+h)=0$ by $d=h+B$. This proves every coefficient cancels, including $K=0$.

Same-component deficiency one, missing above. Here $r\le s$, $P>Q$, and $\varepsilon=(-1)^{s-r}$, obtained by moving the inserted missing threshold from row $s$ to position $r$; the column cofactor has the same sign. If $r=1$, all inward row positions are at most $q_1<p_1$ and cannot fill the missing top threshold; the first column is zero and any outward repair raises it further, so both sums vanish. For $r\ge2$ the only unique row sources are $i\le r-1$, with $M_i=q_i-p_i\ge0$. The direct rows have $R_i=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in(q_i-P',q_i-P]\cap[p_i-Q,p_i-Q')}\phi(d)$. The first column potentials equal $R_i$ for $i\le r-2$, while $C_i^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^{M_i}\phi(h)(1_{Q'<P-h\le Q}-1_{Q'<P'-h\le Q})$. Exchanged rows are $X_i=-\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{M_i}\phi(k)(1_{P\le Q+k<P'}-1_{P\le Q'+k<P'})=-C_i^{\mathrm{second}}$, again by endpoint reciprocity. This exhausts repairs: the duplicate source must be paired with a head row above the missing interval, and outward column repairs must lower an endpoint paired with a unique head column, or use the endpoint pair. The sole residual is at $i=r-1$. Put $M=q_{r-1}-P'\ge0$, $B=P'-P>0$, $A=P-Q>0$, $L=Q-Q'>0$, $I_0=[A,A+L)$, $I_1=I_0+B$. Then $R_{r-1}=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap(M,M+B]}\phi(d)$ and $C_{r-1}^{\mathrm{second}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h=1}^M\phi(h)(1_{I_0}(h)-1_{I_1}(h))$; the endpoint-pair column term is $C^{\mathrm{end}}=\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le M}(\phi(B+h)-\phi(h))$, with positive cofactor because the lowered endpoint is $P$. Thus $R_{r-1}-C_{r-1}^{\mathrm{second}}-C^{\mathrm{end}}=\varepsilon\sum_{d\in I_1\cap[1,M+B]}\phi(d)-\varepsilon\sum_{h\in I_0,\,1\le h\le M}\phi(B+h)=0$. The translation $d=h+B$ is valid since $A>0$.

Same-component deficiency two and higher. At rank $N-2$, the excess threshold copies are one triple or two pairs. Inward row repairs of a triple cannot reach missing thresholds between its source beads. For two pairs with thresholds $r<s$, both missing thresholds must lie strictly between them, say $r<m_1<m_2<s$; otherwise both row and column sums are zero. For columns this follows from $\ell(p_j)=\#\{i:\kappa(q_i)\le j\}$: duplicated row thresholds are jumps, missing thresholds are flats, and outward column repairs require two separate size-two jumps with both flats between. A zero first column also cannot be repaired by raising it. In the active pattern put $Q=q_r>Q'=q_{r+1}$, $R=q_{s-1}>R'=q_s$, $I_1=[P,P')=[p_{m_1},p_{m_1-1})$, $I_2=[S,S')=[p_{m_2},p_{m_2-1})$, $J_Q=(Q',Q]$, $J_R=(R',R]$. The common row/column sign is $\varepsilon=(-1)^{m_1-r+s-1-m_2}$, counted by moving the inserted thresholds to their sorted positions. Switching a source copy or switching the two target thresholds reverses it. Define $A_I(k)=1_{R+k\in I}-1_{R'+k\in I}$ and $B_I(k)=1_{Q-k\in I}-1_{Q'-k\in I}$; define $D_P^\pm(J;k)=1_{P\pm k\in J}-1_{P'\pm k\in J}$ and $D_S^\pm(J;k)=1_{S\pm k\in J}-1_{S'\pm k\in J}$. The complete row coefficient of $\phi(k)$ is $\varepsilon(A_{I_1}(k)B_{I_2}(k)-A_{I_2}(k)B_{I_1}(k))$; the column coefficient is $\varepsilon(D_S^+(J_Q;k)D_P^-(J_R;k)-D_P^+(J_Q;k)D_S^-(J_R;k))$. u$ at an actual multipartition weight $

u})=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu
u};$ the empty case $n=0$ gives $0$, all ranks keep the fixed parameters $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, and arbitrary-composition coefficients are combinatorial only.
